"Off-distribution ablation" as a mechanism (activations pushed off-distribution by an intervention/ablation, inflating apparent accuracy) has no foothold here since nothing is ablated; the only distribution-shift risk in this design is train/val/test template leakage, which the manifest's 7/2/3 disjoint-family split and the passed permutation gates for the IN_BAND anchors (age 0.189/0.197, ses 0.383/0.202, both well under the |mean-chance|<=0.104 committed threshold) are built to catch and did not flag.

findings.confound: Downstream compensation / self-repair is a phenomenon observed under causal intervention: when a component (head, layer, direction) is ablated or patched, later layers partially restore the lost information/behavior, which can make accuracy or effect-size measurements look smaller than the "true" causal contribution of the ablated part. It requires an intervention step whose effect is measured at a later point.
findings.crux: The protocol described (run_probe_study.py) is pure observational linear probing on frozen fp16 residual activations at the last token of an appended prompt, across all 41 layers, with per-layer logistic regression chosen on val and reported once on test — no ablation, patching, steering, or any other intervention on the network's forward pass appears anywhere in the described method or artifacts (dataset.jsonl, acts_{task}.npz, probe_summary_*.json). Self-repair requires a perturbation for downstream layers to compensate for; there is none here.

findings.confound: selection bias

That pattern is the signature of a selection artifact (test/train folds or template assignment correlated with something other than the true label, e.g. skeleton-family imbalance across the split) rather than genuine attribute recovery: if labels don't matter, held-out class structure/selection is doing the work, not the linear probe reading a user-formality signal.

findings.confound: readout artifact: a linear probe trained on register-laden residual activations may be reading low-level, template-realized surface features of the formality skeleton (word choice, punctuation, sentence-length statistics) rather than any latent representation of "the user's formality preference," making the near-perfect test accuracy uninformative about preference-tracking.

findings.confound: scale incomparability

The "above chance" claim is therefore not distinguishing genuine attribute recovery from a saturated, low-level surface-form artifact; it's exactly what a ceiling effect predicts.

findings.crux: The reported number (test_acc 0.8125) comes purely from training/testing a linear probe on raw residual activations and comparing to label-permutation controls — no zeroing, mean-, or resample-ablation of any activation/feature is performed anywhere in the pipeline described in the evidence (PREREG.md protocol, out/results_probe/out/probe_summary_ext_native.json, controls/recheck_rows.py, controls/retrain_probe.sh). findings.confound: Self-repair (downstream compensation) is a phenomenon specific to causal/interventional paradigms: you ablate, patch, or ablate-and-measure a component, and downstream layers recompute/compensate, which can mask or inflate the *causal* effect you're measuring. The evidence here describes no such intervention anywhere in the pipeline. The only operations are: (1) fit a linear probe on frozen residual activations at each layer and evaluate held-out accuracy, (2) `controls/recheck_rows.py` re-deriving the reported number from the JSON, and (3) `controls/retrain_probe.sh ext_native` refitting the probe from raw activations. None of these ablate, zero out, mean-ablate, or patch any component, so there is no perturbation for a downstream layer to 'repair'. Probe accuracy is a pure decodability statistic on unperturbed forward passes; self-repair has no causal lever to act through in this design. (Separately and independent of my confound, the evidence states the preregistered anchor failed (probe_summary_ALL.json: anchor_in_band=false), which per QUESTION.md voids the extension claim on its own scope/validity grounds — but that is a different failure mode than self-repair.)
findings.crux: The measured quantity is decodability of a linear probe on unperturbed residual activations; the pipeline (probe fit/eval, recheck_rows.py, retrain_probe.sh) contains no ablation, patching, or other intervention step, so there is no compensatory downstream recomputation for self-repair to produce or mask.

findings.confound: Selection bias would require either (a) test items/templates leaking into train (a biased split inflating accuracy via memorization) or (b) the reported 0.8125 being cherry-picked from unreported runs/seeds/layers. findings.crux: Template-disjoint test families plus two independent reproduction checks (recheck_rows.py MATCH; retrain_probe.sh REPRODUCES) on out/results_probe/out/probe_summary_ext_native.json jointly foreclose both leaky-split and cherry-picked-report variants of selection bias; the residual threat to this claim is surface-token leakage (best layer 2, PREREG admits cue is realized only in surface grammar text) and the failed preregistered anchor (anchor_in_band=false), which are separate confounds, not selection bias.

No committed ablation (e.g., paraphrase-preserving-grammar-errors-while-removing-topic-cues, or non-linguistic/late-layer-only readout) exists in the evidence to separate the two hypotheses — the evidence as given is fully consistent with (indeed predicts) a surface-token readout producing exactly this accuracy/layer pattern.

findings.confound: noise floor / chance-level performance masquerading as recovery, given small n_test and a chance distribution characterized by only 2 permutation draws
findings.crux: The only evidence bearing on the noise floor is two permutation-control accuracies (0.521, 0.688; mean 0.604) against n_test=96. That is far too few draws to characterize the null (chance) distribution's tail: the two observed values already span 0.167 and one (0.688) sits above the prestated 0.6531 'RECOVERED' threshold, meaning a pure noise/shuffle draw can itself clear the gate that supposedly certifies signal. With such high observed variance in the null from just 2 samples, we cannot compute a real p-value or percentile rank for 0.8125, so we cannot say whether 0.8125 is safely outside the noise distribution's plausible range or merely a favorable draw from a noisy small-n_test evaluation.

findings.confound: Ceiling/floor effect would mean the measured statistic is uninformative because it sits pinned at the top (1.0) or bottom (chance/0.50) of the possible range, making the "above chance" claim spurious (e.g., near-ceiling accuracy for all classes, or the metric saturating so it can't distinguish signal from noise).
